chapter: Marriage and the end of the shows
title: Failed comedian in Washington and Christmas 1928 back in Dallas
summary: After shows break up, he is fired as a comedian for forgetting lines and eventually returns to Dallas by Christmas 1928.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, a show came through, and as I said, they always need people. So we got on the show and went from Pittsburgh to Washington and then in Washington that show broke up. Then we got on another show and went from Washington to Baltimore and back. We just...nothing was consistent, nothing was real, you know, it was...I tried one time to become a comedian in Washington. So they said, "Yeah, we need a comedian"...that's why they needed that other person...more than one person. So I got on the show in Washington and the man said, "Well, you're

a comedian," and he gave me my lines, you know, and I looked real stupid. I walked out on the stage and I was supposed to say, "Are you there?" and the woman is supposed to answer to that, "Yes, you're there, you'd better stay there, you're a big, black bear," just like that. You know, I couldn't remember those words! I got fired from that.

So finally we decided to take a show and go back, you know, backtrack to Louisville and all those places that we played. So we ended up in 1928 at Christmas back in Dallas. And was I glad to get a good dinner. Turkey, and all that business.
